comments: Third point in the quant_freeze_iters sweep for the leaky0125+2w+1 hardware scheme (see kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_kernel3_finetune_dropout_leaky0125_wq2x1_latefreeze.json's own comments for the first two). freeze=60000 (~58% of ~101600 iters): peaked val dice 0.3468 at epoch 126 then collapsed to trivial all-background by epoch 285. freeze=92000 (~91%): same 0.3468 peak at epoch 126 (deterministically identical up to that point -- both runs share torch_seed/numpy_seed and only diverge once iteration count passes whichever freeze point is smaller), but this time no collapse -- val dice instead plateaued/oscillated in ~0.26-0.30 through epoch 300, never climbing past the shared epoch-126 peak. Under the *old* w=w scheme, the equivalent post-freeze weight-only tail (from ~58% onward) is exactly where the anchor's own dice kept climbing to its final 0.3757 -- so late-freeze here traded collapse for a lost improvement pathway, not just for stability. Hypothesis: an intermediate freeze point might get both -- late enough to avoid the drift-driven collapse, early enough to leave a meaningful weight-only refinement tail. This config only changes quant_freeze_iters 92000 -> 76000 (~75%, roughly the midpoint of the two prior runs) to test that. Not confirmed; only two data points exist so far (both collapsed the low-freeze/high-freeze question into a single before/after comparison at an epoch-126 checkpoint that's identical either way).
